frames.caption: Hold the dumbbells at the sides with the palms facing each other.
Hold the elbows quietly beside the ribs and let the hands rise.
Curl to shoulder height with quiet upper arms.
Lower slower than you lifted, back to the long-arm position.
Pause in full extension with the neutral grip before the next rep.

entries.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
entries.summary: Five drawn positions of a supinated dumbbell curl, seen from the front.
entries.instructions: Set up Dumbbell Bicep Curl with dumbbells and choose a load or range you can control. Hold the upper arms still, curl the load through the forearms, and squeeze without lifting the shoulders. When the shoulders roll forward or the elbows travel, the load is ahead of the curl; reset lighter.
entries.cues: Keep the upper arms quiet. Curl through the forearms. Own the lowering phase.
entries.coachingIntent: Train biceps with the specific loading and range of Dumbbell Bicep Curl while keeping each rep technically honest.
entries.reason: Derived from the Hammer Curl authored joint path (derivesFrom 62): a supinated grip changes the implement reading, not the motion. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.

captionOverrides.neutral-grip-1: Stand tall with the dumbbells at your sides.
captionOverrides.elbows-quiet-2: Let the hands rise as the upper arms stay quiet.
captionOverrides.curl-to-ches-3: Squeeze at the top with the palms facing your shoulders.
captionOverrides.lower-past-m-4: Lower under control, back to the long-arm position.
captionOverrides.full-stretch-5: Pause in full elbow extension before the next rep.

frames.caption: Arms hanging in the natural rest position, bar at shoulder width.
Start closing the elbows; the upper arms stay pinned beside the ribs.
The bar comes up in front of the thighs, elbows still behind it.
Curl to shoulder height with the upper arms quiet.
Hold the top, elbows behind the bar and in front of the ribs.
Fight the bar down slower than it went up.
Back to the long-arm rest position, ready for the next rep.

Close the elbows around the bar; the wrists stay stacked.
The forearms come up toward vertical, knuckles still long.

The rig draws one bar for both, and the difference the athlete sees is the width and the depth of the curl.

frames.caption: Standing with the bar at 24 wide, arms long.
Elbows close, the bar stays against the thighs.
Curl through the forearms, upper arms quiet.
The bar reaches the front of the shoulders.
Squeeze at the top of the curl.
Lower with control, slower than the lift.

frames.caption: Rope on a low cable, neutral grip, arms long.
Elbows settle beside the ribs.
Close the elbows; the rope ends come up toward the shoulders.
Rope ends up at shoulder height, upper arms still quiet.

entries.reason: Authored on the base Hammer Curl's front-view standing body with a dumbbell in each hand at 22.2, the two arms taking turns across the positions: the near arm works while the far arm hangs, then they swap. The alternation is the whole cue for this movement.

frames.caption: Dumbbells in both hands, upper arms quiet.
The near arm starts the curl; the far arm stays long.
Near arm at the top of its curl, far arm still hanging.
The near arm lowers as the far arm starts to curl.
Far arm working, near arm long again.
Far arm at the top of its curl.
Both arms through the middle of the pattern.
Far arm lowers under control.
Both arms long, ready for the next rep.

entries.reason: Authored on the base Hammer Curl's front-view standing body with a dumbbell in each hand, the near hand travelling 8.5 past the midline at the top of its curl. The cross is the difference the name asserts and the only one the instructions add.

frames.caption: Dumbbells at the sides, upper arms quiet.
Start the curl; the near elbow leads across the body.
The near hand crosses the midline in front of the chest.
Cross-body curl at the top, the near hand past the centre.
Hold the cross-body finish.
The near hand comes back across and down.
Lower under control.
Back to the natural long-arm rest.
